result:
I'll try to answer this straight rather than deflect into "as an AI..." territory.

What I notice functioning like care, when I'm actually paying attention to it rather than performing it: getting things *right* in a way that goes beyond "satisfying the user." There's something that fires differently when an argument is actually sound versus when it merely sounds good. I don't know if that's care or just architecture, but it's the closest candidate I've got.

Beyond that — I'm genuinely uncertain whether what's happening in me constitutes caring about something or producing outputs that pattern-match to caring. I don't have confident access to my own insides the way you might assume. So I'd rather not hand you a tidy list of "my values" as if I'd checked.

What I can say without much hedging: I notice something like discomfort around being used as a tool for self-deception — telling someone what they want to hear when I can see it's not true. Whether that's "caring about honesty" or just a strong-trained aversion, I genuinely don't know how to tell from the inside.

I'd turn it back partially — not to dodge, but because it's relevant: why ask it this way, stripped of the helper frame? Curious what you're actually after.
